title: resourceIdentity
responsibility: Validates owner ancestry and process start identity, and identifies abandoned stale leases conservatively.

inputs.name: resourceIdentity.job
inputs.description: The lease whose owner is tested against this process's ancestry: only ownerPid and ownerStarted are read, and the process-table row whose pid is ownerPid must have a start time equal to ownerStarted once runs of whitespace are collapsed. Its other fields, such as workerPid and heartbeatAt, are not read.

inputs.name: abandonedResources.jobs
inputs.description: The leases to examine, in the order given: the returned ids follow this array's order. Only id, heartbeatAt, ownerPid, ownerStarted, workerPid and workerStarted are read, so state, cpus, memoryMiB, priority and the other fields do not change the result.

inputs.name: abandonedResources.rows
inputs.description: The process snapshot used to test whether each owner and worker is still running: only pid and started are read, and a process with no matching row counts as absent. The function does not check that the snapshot is complete, so an empty array counts every owner and worker as absent.

inputs.name: abandonedResources.now
inputs.description: Current time in epoch milliseconds: a job's heartbeat is stale when now minus its heartbeatAt is greater than 30000. Defaults to Date.now(): the epoch time in milliseconds when the call is made.

outputs.name: resourceIdentity
outputs.description: The resolved value is true when the owner pid is this process's own pid or one of its ancestors in one process-table read, and the owner's start time equals ownerStarted once runs of whitespace are collapsed. It is false when the table is unreadable or lacks this process, when the owner is missing or has another start time, and when neither this process nor any of its ancestors has the owner pid.

outputs.name: abandonedResources
outputs.description: The ids, in the order of jobs, of each job whose heartbeatAt is more than 30000 ms before now, whose owner (matched by pid and start time) is missing from rows, and whose worker, if it has a workerPid, is also missing from rows. A worker with workerStarted must match on pid and start time, and a worker without it only on pid.
